    # (in many religions, often [[capitalisation|capitalized]], inexact) Synonym of [[:underworld#English|underworld]], an [[:underground#English|underground]] [[:land#English|land]] of the [[:dead#English|dead]] without [[:eternal#English|eternal]] [[:punishment#English|punishment]] or with [[:only#English|only]] [[:some#English|some]] [[:region#English|region]]s of [[:punishment#English|punishment]]. =====Usage notes===== In English, ''Hell'' or ''hell'' is typically conflated with present Christian and Islamic beliefs about a fiery [[underworld]] of eternal punishment inflicted by [[demon]]s on the wicked, which may or may not include [[Limbo]], a realm for the virtuous dead of other faiths. Similar beliefs in other traditions are often—but not univerally—distinguished by using specific alternative names (e.g. ''[[w:Diyu|Diyu]]'' for the traditional Chinese underworld of punishments for the wicked) or by distinguishing the specific form of ''hell'' intended, as with calling [[Naraka]] the ''[[Buddhist]] Hell'' or ''Hells''. Often within these traditions and occasionally within Christian and Islamic sects, the land of punishment is only a temporary realm of purification of the spirit, similar to [[Purgatory]] in [[Catholicism]]. Informally, any underground [[afterworld]] may be called ''Hell'' but scholarly treatment usually distinguishes such neutral and general beliefs as the Hebrew [[Sheol]], the Greco-Roman [[Hades]], and Sumerian [[Kur]] with more neutral terms, such as [[:underworld#English|underworld]], [[:afterlife#English|afterlife]], or ''[[land]] of the [[dead]]''. =====Synonyms===== * ''See'' '''[[Thesaurus:afterlife]]''' =====Descendants===== * → Korean: [[:헬#Korean|헬]] (hel) =====Translations=====
